Eaton heavy-duty truck transmission antitrust lawsuit appeals court 2026 status

findings.claim: Eaton's FY2026 Form 10-Q (filed for the quarter ended 2026-06-30) discloses that the company is subject to various antitrust and trade regulation claims, and states management believes these matters will not have a material adverse effect on the condensed consolidated financial statements.
findings.source: Eaton Corp plc Form 10-Q FY2026 (SEC EDGAR, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001551182/000155118226000030/etn-20260630.htm)

findings.claim: A long-running antitrust suit (Wallach v. Eaton Corp / consolidated truck-buyer claims) alleges Eaton and heavy-duty truck manufacturers conspired to maintain Eaton's near-monopoly of heavy-duty truck transmissions from 2002 to 2014; a federal appeals court restored the truck buyers' claims and remanded the case to the U.S. District Court in Wilmington, Delaware, and as of a December 2025 update the case remained in the discovery phase.
findings.source: TT News: Appeals Court Restores Antitrust Suit Against Eaton and Every Heavy-Duty Truck Maker in North America (https://www.ttnews.com/articles/appeals-court-restores-antitrust-suit-against-eaton-and-every-heavy-duty-truck-maker-north)

findings.claim: In 2021 the DOJ's Antitrust Division sued to block Danfoss A/S's proposed $3.3 billion acquisition of Eaton's hydraulics business (Civil Action No. 1:21-cv-1880, D.D.C., filed 2021-07-14); the matter was resolved via a settlement requiring divestitures of both companies' orbital motor and hydraulic steering unit manufacturing businesses, and a final judgment was subsequently entered, allowing the transaction to close.
findings.source: DOJ Antitrust Division case page, U.S. v. Danfoss A/S and Eaton Corporation Plc (https://www.justice.gov/atr/case/us-v-danfoss-and-eaton-corporation-plc)

regulatory_antitrust.note: No evidence found of any new (2026) antitrust or breakup-risk investigation targeting Eaton's current electrical/industrial segments. The only live matter is the legacy heavy-duty truck transmission case (pre-2015 conduct, immaterial to current Electrical/Aerospace-driven thesis); the Danfoss hydraulics matter is closed (2021 divestiture settlement, hydraulics business itself was later divested by Eaton in 2021 per that same transaction).

queries_run: Eaton Corporation tariff exposure electrical products supply chain 2026 earnings call
Eaton Corporation export control entity list China 2026

findings.claim: Eaton's Electrical Americas segment has faced cost pressure from the 2026 Section 232 tariff backdrop: Section 232 steel and aluminum tariffs were raised to 50% in mid-2025, and a 50% Section 232 copper tariff took effect 2025-08-01; these inputs feed Eaton's electrical equipment manufacturing (wire, busway, switchgear).
findings.source: Eaton price increase / tariff coverage, getuniqcli.com "Eaton Price Increase 2026: Power Lead Times Are the Real Story" (https://getuniqcli.com/news/eaton-price-increase-2026)

findings.claim: On 2026-02-20 the U.S. Supreme Court ruled to invalidate certain tariffs imposed under IEEPA, and the Court of International Trade subsequently ordered CBP to develop a refund process; Eaton stated in its filings that it was still evaluating the financial impact and could not reasonably estimate the amount, timing, or collectability of any refunds.
findings.source: Flexport: The Supreme Court's IEEPA Tariff Ruling (https://www.flexport.com/blog/the-supreme-courts-ieepa-tariff-ruling-next-steps-potential-refunds-and/); corroborated by Eaton Q2 2026 earnings disclosure

findings.claim: In Eaton's Q2 2026 earnings disclosure, the net IEEPA tariff refund impact was less than $3 million in the quarter (management characterized as less than $0.01 of EPS), and full-year 2026 tariff impacts are already embedded in guidance and considered immaterial to consolidated results.
findings.source: Eaton (ETN) Q2 2026 Earnings Call Transcript, The Globe and Mail (https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/markets/stocks/ETN/pressreleases/3731391/eaton-etn-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/)

findings.claim: Eaton has committed $1 billion across 24 capacity-expansion projects within Electrical Americas to scale U.S. production output, framed by management as addressing both strong data-center/grid demand and supply-chain/tariff-related cost pressure.
findings.source: Eaton investor materials / earnings coverage (Trefis ETN data page and Q1 2026 analyst presentation, https://www.eaton.com/content/dam/eaton/company/investor-relations/quarterly-earnings/filings/2026/q1/q1-2026-analyst-presentation.pdf)

reg_tariff_export.note: No evidence found that Eaton or its named suppliers/customers are on the U.S. Entity List or China's export control/unreliable-entity lists; a 2026-06-22 China export-control list addition targeted ten other US entities (rare-earth/drone-related), not Eaton. Eaton's tariff exposure is real but management states 2026 guidance already absorbs it as immaterial, and the IEEPA ruling is a net-positive optionality (potential refunds) rather than a new cost.
